card: This PR defines a long timeout attribute (at least 60 seconds) in the IPC mining functional test and applies it to waits that depend on test-triggered events. On slow machines or heavily loaded CI runners, short 1-second defaults cause intermittent timeouts before triggered actions take effect. The author provides a reproduction patch demonstrating the race on master, following up on merged PR 36791.
changed_since_previous: Diff provided (previously nopatch); the implementation adds `self.long_ipc_timeout` and consolidates timeout definitions across multiple wait calls in the test.
evidence: Follow-up to #36791 pointing out an identical race condition in the `template6` `waitNext` call.
Author supplies a reproduction patch demonstrating failure on master by inserting a 1.2s delay before sending the self-transfer.
problem: On slow test hosts or busy CI environments, event-driven waits in the IPC mining test can hit their 1-second default timeout and fail intermittently before the test's asynchronous action triggers the expected event.

risk.why: Touches only functional test timeout parameters in interface_ipc_mining.py.

summary: Defines a dedicated `self.long_ipc_timeout` attribute (at least 60 seconds) in `interface_ipc_mining.py` and applies it to wait calls expected to complete via an explicit test-triggered event. This replaces shorter or inconsistently scaled timeouts on IPC wait calls.
